as_of: October 2026 snapshot with a 2025 full year flow baseline
as_of_note: Capacities include the expansions completed in May 2026 (Gray Oak) and August 2026 (Cactus III). Export and EIEC loading anchors are 2025 full year. East Daley utilization covers the 12 months to August 2026, with a latest three month read beside it. The 2026 episode export rate is carried as its own card and is not blended with the 2025 rate.

corridors.label: Permian to Corpus Christi and Ingleside
corridors.note: The shortest Permian to salt water pipe run on the Gulf Coast. Combined nameplate is 2,715 after the 2026 expansions. Three of the four pipes were built in 2019 and 2020 mainly to serve exports, which is why Corpus is the marginal US export point.

corridors.label: Eagle Ford to Corpus Christi
corridors.note: Local gathering feeding the refineries and the Inner Harbor. The Corpus bound share is not published. The competing eastbound leg, Kinder Morgan KMCC at 350 nameplate, takes Eagle Ford barrels to Houston and is outside this hub.
corridors.to: Corpus Christi refineries and Inner Harbor terminals

corridors.label: Corpus Christi crude exports
corridors.note: Crude exports were about 2,200 in 2025, over half of all US crude exports, and ran at about 2,500 during the 2026 episode against a Port stated pipeline limited ceiling of about 2,600. The pipes, not the docks or the tanks, are the constraint.
corridors.to: International markets, with Europe and Asia named in the dossier

corridors.label: Waterborne receipts into Corpus Christi
corridors.note: Imports and coastwise receipts feeding the refineries, including Mexican grades named in Valero reporting. Small next to exports, and not yet reduced to a series for this hub.

demand.label: Flint Hills Resources Corpus Christi
demand.note: West and East plants combined at about 300, with the West plant crude unit at about 230 per Reuters. This is the complex refinery of the three, with coking capacity, and it runs Eagle Ford crude plus heavier and imported grades fed by Koch system pipes from the Eagle Ford. One Reuters quote cited 363 for this plant, which conflicts with the company figure of about 300 and is treated in the dossier as an error in that quote. Crude runs by plant are not published at hub level, so this item is capacity only.
demand.source: Flint Hills Resources company figure for the complex total; Reuters 2023 plant reporting for the West plant crude unit

demand.label: Valero Bill Greehey, Corpus Christi
demand.note: Complex conversion refinery, West plant from 1983 plus the East plant acquired in 2001. Sources conflict on capacity, so the item ships as a range on purpose and no single point is chosen. It runs Eagle Ford crude, Permian crude delivered on the Cactus system, and imported grades including Mexican crude. Crude runs by plant are not published at hub level, so this item is capacity only.
demand.source: Reuters at 290; offshore-technology at 315; CLUI at 325. EIA Refinery Capacity Report is the pinning source, not yet pulled for this plant

demand.label: CITGO Corpus Christi
demand.note: East and West plants combined. Gasoline heavy yield at about 60 percent gasoline per Scotia and CITGO asset summaries. It runs light sweet crude including Eagle Ford crude. Sources differ slightly on capacity, so the item ships as a range. Crude runs by plant are not published at hub level, so this item is capacity only.
demand.source: Reuters and TCEQ filing October 2026 at 165; Scotia CITGO asset review at 167.5

demand.label: Enbridge Ingleside Energy Center (EIEC)
demand.note: Loaded 415.4 MMbbl in 2025, about 1,138 per day and about 52 percent of the Port total for 2025. This is the one hard flow number on the export side. Storage is about 20 MMbbl after Phase VII added 2.5 MMbbl. Four deepwater docks and a loading rate of 160,000 barrels per hour, claimed by Enbridge as the fastest on the US Gulf Coast. It receives Gray Oak, Cactus I, Cactus II, Cactus III and Harvest barrels.
demand.source: Enbridge 2026 story on EIEC, company reported 2025 loadings and Phase VII storage

demand.label: South Texas Gateway (STG)
demand.note: Gibson Energy owns STG, acquired in August 2023 for about US$1.1 billion. Storage is 8.6 MMbbl and there are two deepwater docks. The 800 figure is rated throughput as published by Buckeye at start up, not an actual loading rate. Gibson cited 1,000 of authorized throughput at acquisition, which is an authorized figure on a different basis and is not used as the nameplate here. It receives Gray Oak, Cactus II and Cactus III barrels. Actual loadings are not published.
demand.source: Gibson Energy and Buckeye releases 2020 to 2023 for storage and rated throughput; Gibson acquisition release August 2023
demand.vintage: Rated throughput as published at start up and at the 2023 acquisition

demand.label: EPIC Marine Terminal (Plains, with Cactus III)
demand.note: Two Aframax class docks at Ingleside, now held by Plains with Cactus III. The terminal is a Platts approved delivery point for WTI Midland into Dated Brent. Its storage sits inside the Cactus III system total of about 7 MMbbl, which includes about 3.5 MMbbl at Robstown inland, so no separate terminal storage figure ships. No rated daily throughput and no actual loadings are published for this dock.
demand.source: EPIC Crude Holdings releases 2022; Plains reporting on the Cactus III acquisition

demand.label: Inner Harbor terminals (Pin Oak, Eagle Ford Terminals, NuStar North Beach, Buckeye Texas Partners)
demand.note: Smaller docks up the ship channel that serve the refineries, Eagle Ford barrels and the coastwise and barge trade. The dossier does not size these terminals, so no capacity, storage or flow figure ships for this item.
demand.source: RBN Energy terminal survey series for the terminal names and roles, as cited in the Corpus Christi dossier section 5 item X4

demand.label: Port of Corpus Christi crude exports (control total)
demand.note: Control total, not an extra terminal. Do not add it to EIEC or the other terminals, because EIEC loadings are inside this total. The Port handled over half of all US crude exports in 2025, against a US total of about 4,000 per EIA. The 2026 episode rate of about 2,500 and the Port stated pipeline limited ceiling of about 2,600 are separate vintages carried in the cards, and neither is blended into this 2025 number. This is a memo item and is excluded from card sums.
demand.source: Port of Corpus Christi 2025 results; EIA March 2026 release on 2025 trade for the US total

groups.label: Ingleside
groups.note: The three Ingleside export docks against the inbound Permian pipes. Group value is null because the members carry mixed states: EIEC has a measured 2025 loading value of 1,138, STG is capacity only at a rated 800, and the EPIC dock publishes no flow or rated throughput. Adding the members would mix a flow with capacities.

groups.label: Inner Harbor
groups.note: The up channel terminals plus the three refineries. Group value is null because the terminal item is missing any size and the refinery items are capacity only or ranges.

groups.label: Permian sourced inbound
groups.note: The four Permian long haul pipes. Group value is null because every member is capacity only. Their nameplates sum to 2,715, which is the nameplate card, and a nameplate sum is not a flow.

groups.label: Eagle Ford sourced inbound
groups.note: Eagle Ford gathering plus the Eagle Ford receipt shares of Gray Oak and Cactus III. Group value is null because the gathering item is missing a system number and neither pipe publishes its Eagle Ford receipt share.

groups.label: Refinery pull
groups.note: The three Corpus refineries. Group value is null because one member is capacity only and two are ranges. Combined capacity is about 755 to 790 per the dossier, carried in the refining capacity cards. The often quoted figure of nearly 850 for the Corpus area includes Valero Three Rivers at about 93, which is Eagle Ford in basin refining and is not booked in this hub.

groups.label: Waterborne out
groups.note: All crude leaving Corpus by ship. The group value is the Port control total, not a sum of the terminal members, because only EIEC publishes its loadings. EIEC at 1,138 is about 52 percent of this total.
groups.source: Port of Corpus Christi 2025 results, as cited in the Corpus Christi dossier section 5

notes: Corpus Christi is a demand and export hub, not a producing basin. It produces essentially nothing, so in region production is 0.0 and every barrel in this balance arrives by pipe or ship and leaves by refinery or ship. Supply items are inbound pipes by origin; demand items are refineries by plant and export terminals by dock.

Demand on this feed means metered loadings and plant capacity, not nominations or wants. Refinery items are capacity because Corpus crude runs by plant are not published. Nothing here is a want dressed as a flow.

Cards footing: nameplate 2,715 is the sum of the four Permian long haul nameplates (Gray Oak 1,020 plus Cactus II 670 plus Cactus III 725 plus Cactus I 300). Eagle Ford gathering is unsized and adds nothing to that sum. Effective 2,600 is the Port stated pipeline limited ceiling from 2026, carried as the effective card following the dossier template mapping in section 8.

supply_kbd is null on purpose. Every inbound pipe is capacity only, Eagle Ford gathering is missing a system number, and waterborne receipts have no split series. The only flow anchors on the supply side are the East Daley modelled utilization percentages printed on each pipe item, which are not converted into flows because Cactus III changed nameplate partway through the utilization window.

demand_kbd is null on purpose. The demand items that carry values are EIEC loadings at 1,138 and the Port export control total at 2,200, and the second contains the first, so adding valued demand items would double count. Refinery demand is a capacity range of about 755 to 790, carried in the refining capacity cards, and the other terminals publish no loadings. The balance card is therefore also null: there is no defensible single supply flow to set against a single demand flow in this snapshot.

in_region_demand_kbd is null because refinery capacity is a range, not a point: Flint Hills at about 300, Valero as a range of 290 to 325, and CITGO as a range of 165 to 167.5. The dossier prints the combined total as about 755 to 790. imports_kbd is null because waterborne receipts cannot be split out of the combined Port tonnage. utilization_pct is null at hub level because utilization is a per pipe figure in this hub and the four pipes range from 89 to 100 percent on the East Daley modelled LTM read.

Vintages are not blended. Exports at 2,200 and EIEC loadings at 1,138 are 2025 full year. The episode rate of about 2,500 and the ceiling of about 2,600 are 2026 figures from the Port, carried as separate cards. Pipe nameplates are current to August 2026, after both 2026 expansions.

Canada note, in plain language: no pipeline path from Alberta to Corpus Christi exists. Canadian export pipes end at Cushing, the Chicago and Flanagan area, and onward to Nederland, Port Arthur, Freeport and Texas City. Every Canadian barrel that reaches salt water on the Gulf loads at Houston area, Beaumont and Nederland, or Louisiana docks, or it loads at Westridge on the Pacific. Corpus is on none of those routes, and there is no large Houston to Corpus crude pipeline to complete a detour. Corpus still matters to Canada through price: Corpus clears the marginal US light barrel into Europe and Asia, so when Corpus pipes are full and Permian barrels back up, WTI Midland weakens, Houston follows, and the whole US Gulf Coast light complex softens against Brent, which is the market WCS competes in at the margin. Corpus belongs in the price corridor layer for the WCSB balance, not in the egress stack.

Gray Oak nameplate is a total system figure. The pipe also delivers to Sweeny, outside this hub, so hub inbound is lower than 1,020 for that pipe by an amount that is not published. That gap is most of the residual balancing line.

Draft runs the export side. The ship channel was deepened to 54 feet in June 2025. Suezmax tankers at about 1.0 MMbbl now load fully at Ingleside. VLCCs at about 2.0 MMbbl load only partway at berth and finish offshore by reverse lightering. LOOP in Louisiana remains the only US terminal that fully loads a VLCC at berth.

Extra cards used in this feed: refining_capacity_min_kbd and refining_capacity_max_kbd carry the refinery capacity range; exports_episode_2026_kbd carries the 2026 episode export rate; export_ceiling_kbd carries the Port stated pipeline limited export ceiling; eiec_loadings_kbd repeats the EIEC item value so the one hard export flow is visible at card level.

prices.label: WTI Midland assessment
prices.note: No WTI Midland print is carried in the dossier and none is held, so no value ships. Do not fabricate one.
prices.source: Platts assessed series, not held. The EPIC Marine Terminal is a Platts approved delivery point for WTI Midland into Dated Brent, per EPIC 2022

prices.label: WCS Houston differential
prices.note: WCS is priced and delivered at Houston, not at Corpus, and the dossier carries no print. The item is listed because Corpus sets the light crude price corridor that WCS competes against, not because a Corpus WCS price exists.
prices.source: Assessed series (Argus and Platts class), not held in this feed

prices.label: VLCC reverse lightering cost at Corpus Christi
prices.note: The channel is 54 feet deep, so a VLCC loads only partway at berth, roughly two thirds to three quarters of a full cargo, then tops off offshore by reverse lightering from shuttle tankers. That second handling is a real per barrel cost that LOOP in Louisiana does not pay. Published estimates of the cost vary and none was verified for the dossier, so no figure ships.
prices.source: Broker and charterer reporting (Argus and Platts class sources), not held

storage.note: No hub storage total and no storage level ship. The known pieces are EIEC at about 20 MMbbl after Phase VII, STG at 8.6 MMbbl, and the Cactus III system at about 7 MMbbl in total, of which about 3.5 MMbbl sits at Robstown inland rather than at the dock. Inner Harbor terminal storage is not sized in the dossier, and the Cactus III figure is a system figure rather than a terminal figure, so the pieces do not add to a defensible hub capacity. No inventory level is published in the dossier.
storage.source: Enbridge Q1 2026 for EIEC; Gibson Energy for STG; EPIC Crude Holdings releases for the Cactus III system

supply.label: Gray Oak (Corpus leg)
supply.note: Total system nameplate after the two phase expansion of 120 finished in May 2026, up from 900 at start up in 2019. The pipe takes Permian receipts at Wink and Midland plus Eagle Ford receipts, and delivers to Ingleside, Corpus terminals and Sweeny. The delivery split between Corpus and Sweeny is not public, so the Corpus share of the 1,020 is not stated. Utilization is an East Daley modelled figure: 89 percent over the 12 months to August 2026 and 96 percent in the latest three months.
supply.source: Enbridge Q1 2026 and RBN Energy 2026-09-04 for capacity and the expansion; East Daley Daley Note 2026-08-27 for utilization
supply.vintage: Capacity as of May 2026; utilization 12 months to August 2026

supply.label: Cactus II
supply.note: Runs from the Delaware and Midland area at Wink through Taft to Ingleside and Corpus, and ties into EIEC and STG. Plains holds 70 percent and operates it; Enbridge holds 30 percent. Utilization is an East Daley modelled figure: 100 percent over the 12 months to August 2026 and 101 percent in the latest three months. The latest three month print sits above nameplate because the rating is conservative and the pipe ran over it. No monthly flow series is published; FERC Form 6 is annual only.
supply.source: Plains and Enbridge release 2022-11-02 for capacity and ownership; East Daley Daley Note 2026-08-27 for utilization
supply.vintage: Capacity as of 2026; utilization 12 months to August 2026

supply.label: Cactus III (ex EPIC Crude)
supply.note: Nameplate rose from the 600 to 650 range to 725 when a 75 expansion entered service in August 2026. Plains acquired EPIC Crude and renamed the pipe Cactus III. Receipts are Permian at Orla, Wink, Midland and Crane plus Eagle Ford receipts at Gardendale. A trade press split, single source and flagged in the dossier, puts deliveries at about 250 to Corpus proper and about 400 to Ingleside; the split is not carried as separate items. System storage is about 7 MMbbl, including about 3.5 MMbbl at the Robstown terminal inland. Utilization is an East Daley modelled figure: 91 percent over the 12 months to August 2026 and 101 percent in the latest three months.
supply.source: Plains 2Q26 results and East Daley Daley Note 2026-08-27 for the expansion to 725; EPIC Crude Holdings releases 2022 for the system as built
supply.vintage: Capacity as of August 2026; utilization 12 months to August 2026

supply.label: Cactus I
supply.note: Runs from Midland to Gardendale, in service since 2015, with onward connections to Corpus through Plains and Harvest systems. The split of barrels on the onward leg is not published. Utilization is an East Daley modelled figure: 90 percent over the 12 months to August 2026 and 96 percent in the latest three months.
supply.source: Plains for capacity; East Daley Daley Note 2026-08-27 for utilization
supply.vintage: Capacity as of 2026; utilization 12 months to August 2026

supply.label: Eagle Ford gathering, Corpus bound
supply.note: In basin gathering moves Eagle Ford crude south to Corpus refineries and Inner Harbor terminals, but no source publishes the gathering systems as one Corpus bound number, so no capacity or flow ships for this item. Basin crude production is about 1,000 in total, which is a basin figure, not a Corpus bound flow, and is not used as this item value. The eastbound Kinder Morgan KMCC leg at 350 nameplate takes Eagle Ford barrels to Houston, not Corpus, and is not counted here. The Corpus versus Houston split is the weakest quantified part of this balance.
supply.source: Corpus Christi dossier section 3 item S5, from operator system descriptions for Plains Eagle Ford JV, Enterprise South Texas Crude, Harvest Midstream, NuStar South Texas, Koch and Flint Hills lines and Double Eagle; EIA DPR and Texas RRC class estimates for basin production

supply.label: Waterborne receipts (imports and coastwise)
supply.note: Foreign and domestic cargoes land at refinery docks and are small next to exports. Port crude shipments totalled 127.4 million short tons in 2025, which against about 2,200 of exports implies total crude waterborne movement of about 2,400 to 2,500. That combined figure cannot be split into an imports number from the sources in the dossier, so no imports value ships.
supply.source: Port of Corpus Christi annual reportage for 2025 crude shipment tonnage; cargo level series held in the AIS tanker database, not yet reduced for this hub
supply.vintage: 2025 full year for the tonnage anchor

supply.label: Residual between inbound nameplate and the Port effective ceiling (balancing line)
supply.note: Balancing line, printed and named, not a measured flow. Permian long haul nameplate of 2,715 minus the Port stated effective ceiling of about 2,600 leaves about 100 to 150. The dossier attributes this gap to the Gray Oak share delivered outside Corpus, mainly to Sweeny, plus normal derates. It is a memo item and is excluded from card sums.
supply.source: Corpus Christi dossier sections 3 and 8; Port of Corpus Christi 2026 for the effective ceiling
